title: LeWM Push-T on dataset-defined reachable tasks (random-task confounder removed)
design: shim dataset driving World.evaluate(dataset=...) with real same-episode start/goal pairs; pixels re-rendered locally at 224x224

predecessor.confounder_removed: tasks were randomly sampled and not guaranteed reachable

config.task_source: public partial Parquet shard, same episode, 25 steps apart

baseline_comparison.experiment: KW-LEWM-0002 scaler condition (random tasks, identical planner and scaler)

K1_task_source_matters.detail: block interaction rate 0.75 vs baseline 0.375; displacement median 0.00 -> 27.91

statistical_caveat.issue: n=8 point estimate carries almost no information
statistical_caveat.supported_conclusion: qualitative only: reachable tasks unlock valid control, random tasks do not

methodological_finding.claim: task reachability is a confounder whose magnitude exceeds model differences
methodological_finding.evidence: same checkpoint, planner and scaler; block displacement median 0.0 -> 27.91 and success 0/8 -> 3/8 purely from task source
methodological_finding.implication: world-model success rates reported on randomly paired tasks may mostly reflect task construction, not model capability
methodological_finding.relevance: directly on KineWorld's evaluation/benchmark methodology line

non_monotonicity_note: success does not track block displacement monotonically (ep19 disp 0.79 succeeds, ep191 disp 53.27 fails) because success uses the joint 4-D agent+block pose distance
residual_approximations: scaler fitted on a partial shard (80,384 rows), not the official full training set
pixels re-rendered locally, not the dataset's recorded pixels
allowed_claim: Under a disclosed lite protocol, the official LeWM Push-T checkpoint produced valid closed-loop control on dataset-defined reachable tasks: 3/8 succeeded with zero out-of-play excursions, versus 0/8 and 25% out-of-play on randomly sampled tasks with everything else held fixed.
forbidden_claims: comparison with JEPA-WM or any competitor (no same-protocol control group)
